title: K-Nearest Neighbors & Support Vector Machines — Neighbors or a Safety Fence
key_insight: K-nearest neighbors uses the first idea. A support vector machine uses the second, building a boundary from the closest examples.
body:
## Neighbors or a Safety Fence

A new fruit sits near several labeled fruits on a table. You can ask its nearest neighbors, or draw a fence that leaves the widest gap between fruit groups.

K-nearest neighbors uses the first idea. A support vector machine uses the second, building a boundary from the closest examples.

Both depend on distance, so centimeters and kilograms must be put on comparable scales before either method can judge closeness fairly.
common_mistakes: Using either method before scaling features.
Choosing K or kernel settings on the test set.
Assuming KNN training is costly while ignoring its prediction-time search.
mini_exercise: Draw the situation from “Neighbors or a Safety Fence” with three labeled steps, then explain what changes at each step.
real_world_usage: These contrasting methods teach how distance, boundaries, and scaling shape classification.
explain_back_prompt: Using the “Neighbors or a Safety Fence” story, explain K-Nearest Neighbors & Support Vector Machines without assuming the listener knows machine learning.
